Part A — Creating Vectors and List:
Question #1:

A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total. The following list shows their ages: `34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.

Create a vector for the worker’s age.
(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)
print(age)
```

How many data points?
(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)
length(age)
```
c: Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.

(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)
min(age)
max(age)
```
Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)
selected <- age[c(13:18, 33:35)]
print(selected)
```

Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)

```
f: Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.

(Your answer here)
```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.)
```

Question #2:

R has actually lots of built-in datasets.
For example, the rivers data “gives the lengths (in miles) of 141 “major” rivers in North America, as compiled by the US Geological Survey”.

Use data(rivers)
Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
(Your answer here)
```{r}
rivers <- c(
Length = length(rivers),
Sum = sum(rivers),
Mean = mean(rivers),
Median = median(rivers),
Variance = var(rivers),
 Standard_Deviation = sd(rivers),
Minimum = min(rivers),
Maximum = max(rivers)
)
print(rivers)
```

What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
(Your answer here
it is tabled, amazing

Forbes Ranking

```{r}
powerranking <- c(1:25)

)
```

Question #4:

Create a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.
(Your answer here)



Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?
(Your answer here)


b. How many datapoints do you have?

(Your answer here)



Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
(Your answer here)



How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?  

```{r}
# Question 4: Create a list of 10 vegetables

vegetables <- c(
  "Kangkong",
  "Pechay",
  "Malunggay",
  "Ampalaya",
  "Talong",
  "Sitaw",
  "Kalabasa",
  "Sayote",
  "Okra",
  "Upo"
)

# Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables

vegetables <- c(vegetables, "Mustasa", "Patola")

# Display the result
vegetables

# How many datapoints do you have?
length(vegetables)

# Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5

vegetables <- append(
  vegetables,
  c("Labanos", "Baguio Beans", "Repolyo", "Mais"),
  after = 5
)

# Display the updated vegetable list
vegetables

# How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
```
